objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient who presents with chronic joint pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve had worsening pain in my left great toe, hips, and knees for several years—it's worse when I’m active and gets better when I rest. I also have diabetes, hypertension, obesity, and I’ve been a smoker.
How old are you, and is the pain in your great toe at the base of the toe or the tip?

Doctor: How old are you, and is the pain in your great toe at the base of the toe or the tip? Patient: I’m 69 years old, and the pain in my left great toe is mainly around the base where it meets the foot, not so much at the tip.
Is the stiffness in your joints worse in the morning, and if so, how long does it take to loosen up—less than 30 minutes or more than an hour?
Patient: Yes, I do feel some stiffness when I wake up, but it usually improves after I start moving—around 20–30 minutes, not more than an hour.
Have you ever had episodes where the great toe suddenly became red, hot, and extremely painful for days at a time, or has the pain been consistently achy without those acute flare-ups?
Patient: No, I haven’t had episodes where the toe suddenly turns red and hot with extreme pain for days; it’s been more of a steady, achy pain that worsens with activity.
Have you developed any bony bumps or enlargements at the joints of your fingers, particularly near your fingernails or in the middle of your fingers?

Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any bony bumps or enlargements in my fingers near the fingernails or anywhere else. My trouble is mainly in the left great toe at the base and the hips and knees, especially with activity.
Do you feel or hear any grinding, cracking, or popping sensations in your knees or hips when you move them?
Patient: I don’t notice grinding or cracking, but I do feel pain and stiffness when I move, especially with activity, and it eases once I rest.
Are both your hips and both knees affected, or is it just one side? And is the pain symmetrical (similar on both sides)?

Doctor: Are both your hips and both knees affected, or is it just one side? And is the pain symmetrical (similar on both sides)? Patient: It’s mostly on my left side—my left hip and left knee bother me more than the right. The left great toe is the main problem, and overall it doesn’t feel very symmetrical.
Do any of these joints appear swollen, or have you noticed a decrease in how far you can bend the great toe upward (like when walking)?

Patient: I do notice some swelling around the base of my left great toe, and bending it upward feels more limited—walking feels harder because the toe won’t lift as well. My left hip and knee also feel stiff and a bit swollen at times, mainly when I’ve been active.
Have you ever had a rash with silvery scales, particularly on your elbows, knees, or scalp, or noticed any pitting or ridging in your fingernails or toenails?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any rash with silvery scales on my elbows, knees, or scalp, and I haven’t seen pitting or ridging of my nails.

Doctor: Have you had any significant injury to the affected joints, or any recent infections—like fever, skin infection, or a urinary infection? Patient: I don’t recall any specific injury, fevers, or recent infections.
Have you ever been told you have high uric acid levels, kidney stones, or noticed any chalky white bumps under the skin around your joints?
Patient: I haven’t been told I have high uric acid levels or kidney stones, and I don’t recall any chalky white bumps under the skin around my joints.
Is the pain in your hip located in the groin area, on the side of your hip, or in your buttock?
Patient: The pain in my left hip is mostly in the groin area, and it also tends to feel worse with activity and better when I rest.
Have you ever taken steroid medications (like prednisone) for long periods, or do you drink alcohol heavily?
Patient: I haven’t taken prednisone or other steroids long-term. I do drink about 10 beers a day.
